description: Deterministic Before Non-Deterministic — SAST tools run first (Pass 2), LLM runs after (Passes 3-5). Never use an LLM where a regex, AST pattern, or rule engine produces the same result.
expect: Pass 2 (SAST) always completes before Pass 3 (triage). No LLM calls for pattern detection.
fix: Move pattern-detectable vulnerabilities to OpenGrep rules. Reserve LLM for cross-file reasoning, false-positive filtering, and business logic analysis.

description: Test Without LLMs — CI never makes a real LLM call; tests use TestModel and FunctionModel with ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS=False
fix: Set ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS=False in conftest.py. Use TestModel or FunctionModel for deterministic agent testing.

description: Breaking Changes Are Free During Dev — no shims, legacy aliases, or deprecation wrappers while in dev mode
expect: No backward-compatibility hacks, unused re-exports, or commented-out code
fix: Delete replaced code outright, rename freely, rewrite broken tests

description: Scope Is Configuration, Not Code — model strings, pricing, prompts, tool specs, and rules are YAML/markdown config, not hardcoded
expect: Behavioral parameters come from config/ files, never literals in Python
fix: Extract hardcoded values to the appropriate config file (settings, pricing, prompts, tool specs)

description: Modular, Reusable, Elegant, Robust — extract on second use; handle edge cases at boundaries; prefer keyword args and sensible defaults
expect: Shared logic in centralised modules; no duplicated implementations across files
fix: Extract shared logic to a single module. Keep functions focused with clear single responsibility.

description: Pipeline Is Infrastructure, Not Intelligence — pipeline.py routes, enforces order, and tracks state, but never reasons or calls an LLM directly
fix: Pipeline orchestrates pass execution order. LLM reasoning is delegated to agents via pass orchestrators (triage.py, holistic.py, config_review.py).

description: Separate Implementation from Registration — tool specs are YAML declarations, runner is execution, agents are reasoning. No layer does another's job.
expect: tools/specs/*.yaml declare commands; tools/runner.py executes them; agents/*.py reason about results
fix: Keep each layer focused: specs declare, runner executes, agents reason, passes orchestrate, models validate.

description: Budget enforcement via PydanticAI UsageLimits — do not build custom budget enforcement in Python
fix: Pass UsageLimits(request_limit=N, total_tokens_limit=N) to agent.run(). CostTracker is for audit logging only.

description: Accuracy Over Volume — one CWE, one agent, one focused question. Every LLM security check targets a single vulnerability class with a specific prompt. No monolithic 'find everything' prompts.
expect: Each CWE that needs LLM reasoning has its own check prompt in the taxonomy. Pass 4 runs one agent call per CWE, not one call per file batch. Progress is reported per CWE.
fix: Split multi-CWE prompts into individual focused checks. Each check reads only relevant files and asks one specific question. Measure recall per CWE against corpus samples.

description: Never Trust LLM-Echoed Identifiers — file paths, line numbers, rule IDs, and indexes must be tracked deterministically in code. Never use LLM-returned identifiers to match results back to source data.
expect: After each agent call, echoed identifiers (file_path, line_number) are overridden with the known-correct values from the original data. No lookup dicts keyed on LLM-returned values. Verdicts are written directly onto the source data structure.
fix: Override LLM-echoed identifiers with the original values immediately after agent.run(). Use positional tracking or write-through to the source dict. The LLM reasons; code does bookkeeping.

description: All LLM Context Is Pre-Materialized Locally — agents never call external tools for file I/O. All file content is read locally and inlined in the prompt via context_builder.py.
fix: Remove tool registration from agents. Use context_builder.py to read files and build prompt content locally. Each agent call is a single LLM request.
